messages:
Lee (FinTech): Hi team — during our nightly reconciliation at 02:00 UTC we started seeing a cascade of 429s. Dashboard shows burst credits at 0 and our requests start failing even though our sustained qps is under our quota. Logs show many short spikes. Any quick mitigation?
Anika - Support: sorry about that. Can you paste the raw error body and any rate headers you saw? example headers: `x-rw-rate-limit`, `x-rw-rate-remaining`, `x-rw-burst-credits` help a lot.
Lee (FinTech): here's a sample error: `\{"error\":\"rate_limit\", \"retry_after_ms\": 800}`. Headers from one request: `x-rw-rate-limit: 400`, `x-rw-rate-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-burst-credits: 0`. We run 10 workers that flush queued items at once, last night one run overlapped with a delayed batch so it doubled the immediate traffic.
Evan (SRE): grabbing account traces now. Ops-Bot: please run account_trace(account_id: "fin-42", window: "2001234400-2001234800").
Ops-Bot: trace result: burst pool drained at 02:01:12 after ~900k tokens in 2 mins. refill rate observed ~0.5 credits/sec; max pool (hosted) = 200 credits for this org.
Anika - Support: that lines up. The short answer: your flush pattern created a token surge that exhausted the burst pool. Once pool=0, the system will enforce 429s until credits trickle back. Two paths: client smoothing + smarter retry, or request a temporary/top-up or consider Dedicated.
Lee (FinTech): can you explain the refill behaviour? timeline we can expect?
Anika - Support: for Hosted accounts refill is conservative for fairness across tenants — roughly 0.5 credits/sec up to your account max. So if you burned ~400 credits it'll take ~800s (~13 minutes) to recover fully. We don't show a countdown in the current dashboard but we can provide an ETA when requested.
Lee (FinTech): we need an automated fix — our cron occasionally overlaps. any server-side options we can enable to smooth bursts?
Ravi (PM): we have a feature flag called "burst-smoothing" for enterprise customers that will server-side amortize short spikes by queueing for a few seconds instead of immediate hard 429. It's gated but we can enable a trial for accounts under support supervision.
Evan (SRE): enabling server-side smoothing requires a short config change and a quick safety limit. If they want to test, we can enable for 24h.
Lee (FinTech): that would be great for a trial. While you enable that can you also suggest client-side changes we can roll out today?
Anika - Support: recommended client changes (fast rollout):
- add a sliding-window limiter across your workers (global token bucket or central coordinator). aim for smoothing window ~= 30s
- stagger cron triggers (offset start times across workers by random 0-15s)
- implement linear backoff on 429 using `retry_after_ms` header, with max cap 10s, and a small random jitter to avoid thundering herd
- if batching, split large batches into sub-batches (e.g., 500 tokens -> 5x100) and send sequentially with tiny sleeps

Quick pseudocode for a coordinator smoothing loop:
```
// central lease-based smoother (very small footprint)
while (true) {
  tokens = leaseTokensFromLocalWindow(maxTokens=300)
  for (job of drainQueue(tokens)) {
    await callApi(job)
    await sleep(random(20,80))
  }
  await sleep(1000) // loop every second
}
```

Lee (FinTech): ok we'll stagger cron and add the sleep in the loop. about the server-side smoothing trial — what's the risk?
Evan (SRE): risk is small; we add brief internal queuing (<=10s) to absorb spikes. We monitor tail latencies and abort if overall system load crests. We'll also put a quota-floor so large sustained spikes still get 429s.
Anika - Support: billing question — can you do a short top-up if we need instant headroom?@Billing Ops?
Billing Ops: we can do a temporary one-off credit top-up. For org fin-42 we can add +500 credits for 90 minutes pending approval. Please confirm the request in-thread and we'll apply.
Lee (FinTech): please apply +500 for 90m so our retries and smoothing take over. we'll follow up to disable after trial.
Billing Ops: applied +500 credits, expiry in 5400s, action: success at 2001234695. you'll see `x-rw-burst-credits` begin at 500 next request.
Lee (FinTech): I see the header change — traffic is recovering. thanks!
Anika - Support: follow-ups: we'll enable the 24h burst-smoothing trial now (toggle on). Evan will monitor and we suggest you still deploy client-side smoothing to be safe. We'll add an account note with suggested thresholds.
Ravi (PM): taking note to evaluate surfacing refill ETA in dashboard and an optional alpha for scheduled credit windows (daily reserved bursts). filing a small ticket.
Lee (FinTech): one more question — does Dedicated change how bursts are handled?
Anika - Support: yes. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity so you'll have predictable throughput and much larger local burst allowance. However Dedicated requires commit and setup. We can set up a sizing call if you're interested.
Lee (FinTech): great — thanks everyone. we'll roll out changes and report back.
Anika - Support: thanks Lee. ping if anything looks off. :thumbsup:
